title: Window Functions: ROW_NUMBER, RANK, LAG, LEAD
what_is_it: A window function computes a value 'over' a set of related rows without collapsing them into fewer rows, the way GROUP BY does. PARTITION BY splits the rows into independent groups for the calculation. ROW_NUMBER gives each row a unique sequential number; RANK and DENSE_RANK handle ties (RANK leaves a gap after a tie, DENSE_RANK doesn't); LAG/LEAD read a previous/next row's value into the current row.
why_it_matters: Window functions answer 'per-group ranking' and 'compared to the row before/after' questions - top N per category, running totals, month-over-month change - without a self-join or a slow correlated subquery, and without losing any of the original rows the way an aggregate GROUP BY would.
output:
name       | price | price_rank
-----------------+-------+------------
 Mechanical Keyboard | 79.99 | 1
 Standing Mat        | 45.00 | 2
 USB-C Hub           | 34.50 | 3
common_mistakes: Forgetting PARTITION BY when you actually want per-group ranks - without it, ROW_NUMBER/RANK number every row against the WHOLE result set, not each group separately. Also confusing RANK and DENSE_RANK: after a two-way tie for 2nd place, RANK's next value is 4 (a gap), DENSE_RANK's is 3 (no gap) - they only ever differ when there's an actual tie.
mini_exercise: Given department employee counts of 3, 2, 2, 0, 0 (most to least staffed), write out by hand what RANK() and DENSE_RANK() would assign to each, then check your answer against sql-window-03 and sql-window-04.
postgres_note: Postgres also has NTILE(n) (splits rows into n roughly-equal buckets) and full support for a window's frame clause (ROWS BETWEEN ...) for rolling calculations like moving averages - both go beyond this module's scope but are worth knowing exist.
